title: FAA Part 107 weather practice questions
description: Free FAA Part 107 weather practice questions: METAR and TAF codes, density altitude, wind shear, stability, icing, thunderstorms and 107.51 limits.

questions.question: Which two automated systems does the FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide name as playing a major role in gathering surface aviation weather observations?

options.A: PIREP and SIGMET
options.B: AWOS and ASOS
options.C: TAF and FB
options.D: AIRMET and FA

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "Automated weather sources, such as the Automated Weather Observing Systems (AWOS), Automated Surface Observing Systems (ASOS), as well as other automated facilities, also play a major role in the gathering of surface observations."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Automated weather sources, such as the Automated Weather Observing Systems (AWOS), Automated Surface Observing Systems (ASOS), as well as other automated facilities, also play a major role in the gathering of surface observations.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the conditions for which the Study Guide says convective SIGMETs are issued?

options.A: Rain showers with surface winds of 20 knots
options.B: Hail at the surface of 1/4 inch in diameter
options.C: Turbulence on the leeward side of a mountain
options.D: Tornadoes

questions.explanation: "Convective SIGMETs are issued for severe thunderstorms with surface winds greater than 50 knots, hail at the surface greater than or equal to ¾ inch in diameter, or tornadoes."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Convective SIGMETs are issued for severe thunderstorms with surface winds greater than 50 knots, hail at the surface greater than or equal to ¾ inch in diameter, or tornadoes.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what does the modifier AUTO in a METAR denote?

options.A: The report came from an automated source
options.B: The report corrects an earlier report that contained an error
options.C: The report is a special report issued between routine reports
options.D: The wind direction is variable

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "If the notation “AUTO” is listed in the METAR/SPECI, the report came from an automated source." A corrected report is marked COR instead.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: If the notation “AUTO” is listed in the METAR/SPECI, the report came from an automated source.

questions.question: In a METAR wind group, what does the Study Guide say follows the wind speed when the winds are gusting?

options.A: The letters VRB
options.B: A separate group of numbers separated by a V
options.C: The letter G, followed by the peak gust recorded
options.D: The letters RMK

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says that when winds are gusting the letter G "follows the wind speed (G26KT)", and that after the G "the peak gust recorded is provided."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: If the winds are gusting, the letter “G” follows the wind speed (G26KT). After the letter “G,” the peak gust recorded is provided.

questions.question: How does the Study Guide say the altimeter setting is reported in a METAR?

options.A: In inches of mercury, as a four-digit group always preceded by the letter A
options.B: In millibars, as a three-digit group preceded by the letter Q
options.C: In hundreds of feet AGL, as a three-digit group
options.D: In degrees Celsius, preceded by the letter M

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: the altimeter setting is "reported as inches of mercury" "in a four-digit number group (A2970)", and "It is always preceded by the letter" A.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Altimeter setting—reported as inches of mercury ("Hg) in a four-digit number group (A2970). It is always preceded by the letter “A.”

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what area is a terminal aerodrome forecast (TAF) established for?

options.A: A 50 nautical mile radius around an airport
options.B: The five statute mile radius around an airport
options.C: An entire state
options.D: Only the runway surface

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "A TAF is a report established for the five statute mile radius around an airport."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: A TAF is a report established for the five statute mile radius around an airport.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how often is a TAF updated?

options.A: Every hour, on the hour
options.B: Twice a day, at 0000Z and 1200Z
options.C: Once a day, at 1200Z
options.D: Four times a day, at 0000Z, 0600Z, 1200Z, and 1800Z

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Each TAF is valid for a 24 or 30-hour time period and is updated four times a day at 0000Z, 0600Z, 1200Z, and 1800Z."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Each TAF is valid for a 24 or 30-hour time period and is updated four times a day at 0000Z, 0600Z, 1200Z, and 1800Z.

questions.question: How does the Study Guide define density altitude?

options.A: The height above ground level shown by a barometric altimeter
options.B: The altitude at which the air becomes saturated
options.C: The altitude in the standard atmosphere corresponding to a particular value of air density
options.D: The altitude above which air density no longer affects performance

questions.explanation: The Study Guide defines density altitude as "the altitude in the standard atmosphere corresponding to a particular value of air density."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: The more appropriate term for correlating aerodynamic performance in the nonstandard atmosphere is density altitude—the altitude in the standard atmosphere corresponding to a particular value of air density.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how does the density of air vary with temperature when the pressure is constant?

options.A: Directly: increasing the temperature increases the density
options.B: It does not vary with temperature
options.C: Inversely: increasing the temperature decreases the density
options.D: Inversely, but only above 12,000 feet

questions.explanation: "Increasing the temperature of a substance decreases its density." The Study Guide adds: "Thus, the density of air varies inversely with temperature. This statement is true only at a constant pressure."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Thus, the density of air varies inversely with temperature. This statement is true only at a constant pressure.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, why is moist air lighter than dry air?

options.A: Water vapor is lighter than air
options.B: Moist air is always at a higher pressure
options.C: Moist air always has a lower temperature
options.D: Moisture raises the dew point above the air temperature

questions.explanation: "Water vapor is lighter than air; consequently, moist air is lighter than dry air." So as the water content increases, "the air becomes less dense, increasing density altitude and decreasing performance."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Water vapor is lighter than air; consequently, moist air is lighter than dry air.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what can an inadvertent microburst encounter result in?

options.A: A steady, smooth climb away from the ground
options.B: Structural icing on the airfoil
options.C: A lower density altitude and better performance
options.D: Terrain impact or flight dangerously close to the ground

questions.explanation: The small UA may meet "a performance-increasing headwind, followed by performance-decreasing downdrafts, followed by a rapidly increasing tailwind. This can result in terrain impact or flight dangerously close to the ground."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: This can result in terrain impact or flight dangerously close to the ground.

questions.question: How does the Study Guide describe the airflow down the leeward side of a mountain?

options.A: It flows smoothly and helps carry an aircraft over the peak
options.B: It follows the contour of the terrain and is increasingly turbulent
options.C: It becomes calm close to the terrain
options.D: It rises in steady upward currents

questions.explanation: "As the air flows down the leeward side of the mountain, the air follows the contour of the terrain and is increasingly turbulent. This tends to push an aircraft into the side of a mountain." The smooth upward flow is on the windward side.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: As the air flows down the leeward side of the mountain, the air follows the contour of the terrain and is increasingly turbulent.

questions.topic: Ceiling, visibility and Part 107 weather limits
questions.question: According to the Study Guide, when are clouds reported as broken?

options.A: When five-eighths to seven-eighths of the sky is covered with clouds
options.B: When the entire sky is covered with clouds
options.C: When one-eighth to two-eighths of the sky is covered with clouds
options.D: When the clouds are more than 12,000 feet above the station

questions.explanation: The Study Guide: "Clouds are reported as broken when five-eighths to seven-eighths of the sky is covered with clouds." "Overcast means the entire sky is covered with clouds."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Clouds are reported as broken when five-eighths to seven-eighths of the sky is covered with clouds.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how does the air at the top of an inversion layer act?

options.A: As a source of strong updrafts that build cumulus clouds
options.B: As a barrier that clears fog and haze from the layer below
options.C: As a lid, keeping weather and pollutants trapped below
options.D: As the level where low-level wind shear always ends

questions.explanation: "When the temperature of the air rises with altitude, a temperature inversion exists." The Study Guide says "The air at the top of the layer acts as a lid, keeping weather and pollutants trapped below."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: The air at the top of the layer acts as a lid, keeping weather and pollutants trapped below.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what happens to small vertical disturbances in a stable atmosphere?

options.A: They tend to become larger, resulting in turbulent airflow
options.B: They dampen out and disappear
options.C: They grow into thunderstorms on a daily basis
options.D: They raise the density altitude

questions.explanation: "A stable atmosphere makes vertical movement difficult, and small vertical disturbances dampen out and disappear." Growth into turbulent airflow happens "In an unstable atmosphere".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: A stable atmosphere makes vertical movement difficult, and small vertical disturbances dampen out and disappear.

questions.topic: Dew point, fog, frost and icing
questions.question: What does the Study Guide say aerodynamic cooling can do to an airfoil?

options.A: Keep the airfoil above freezing when the ambient temperature is below 0 °C
options.B: Remove frost from the airfoil during takeoff
options.C: Raise the dew point of the air flowing over the airfoil
options.D: Lower its temperature to 0 °C even though the ambient temperature is a few degrees warmer

questions.explanation: "Aerodynamic cooling can lower temperature of an airfoil to 0° C even though the ambient temperature is a few degrees warmer." Structural icing needs the temperature where moisture strikes the aircraft to be "0° C or colder."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Aerodynamic cooling can lower temperature of an airfoil to 0° C even though the ambient temperature is a few degrees warmer.

questions.topic: Dew point, fog, frost and icing
questions.question: Which of these is one of the four methods the Study Guide gives by which air can reach the saturation point?

options.A: Air warming as it flows down the leeward side of a mountain
options.B: Air cooling at night through contact with the cooler ground
options.C: Air pressure rising at a single weather station
options.D: Water vapor being removed from the air

questions.explanation: "There are four methods by which air can reach the saturation point." The third: "when air cools at night through contact with the cooler ground, air reaches its saturation point."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Third, when air cools at night through contact with the cooler ground, air reaches its saturation point.

questions.question: Through which three stages does the Study Guide say a thunderstorm cell progresses during its life cycle?

options.A: Cumulus, mature and dissipating
options.B: Cumulus, orographic and dissipating
options.C: Developing, squall line and mature
options.D: Mature, first gust and plow wind

questions.explanation: "A thunderstorm cell during its life cycle progresses through three stages-( 1) the cumulus, (2) the mature, and (3) the dissipating."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: A thunderstorm cell during its life cycle progresses through three stages-( 1) the cumulus, (2) the mature, and (3) the dissipating.

questions.question: How does the Study Guide describe the transition of a thunderstorm cell from one stage to another?

options.A: Abrupt and easy to see from the ground
options.B: Marked by the cloud top reaching 12,000 feet
options.C: Subtle, and virtually impossible to detect visually
options.D: Always complete within 5–15 minutes

questions.explanation: "It is virtually impossible to visually detect the transition from one stage to another; the transition is subtle and by no means abrupt."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: It is virtually impossible to visually detect the transition from one stage to another; the transition is subtle and by no means abrupt.

questions.topic: Ceiling, visibility and Part 107 weather limits
questions.question: From what location does 107.51(c) say the minimum flight visibility is observed?

options.A: From the position of the small unmanned aircraft
options.B: From the nearest airport's weather station
options.C: From the position of the visual observer
options.D: From the location of the control station

questions.explanation: 107.51(c): "The minimum flight visibility, as observed from the location of the control station must be no less than 3 statute miles."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.51, Operating limitations for small unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The minimum flight visibility, as observed from the location of the control station must be no less than 3 statute miles.
